name: Select an implementation while the program runs
description: Lets a program that embeds the package pick its implementation while it runs, without reading this repository, and declare an alternative in one line.
purpose: Choose, inside a running program, which implementation of a solution serves a call, and refuse an unknown name by listing the valid choices.
approach: Resolve the implementation from a per-call name, an environment setting, a deployment table or the project default, and declare alternatives where the code defines them.
out_of_scope: Deciding which implementation is best, and branching on the choice at every call in the embedding program.
milestones: 1. Runtime selection: the selector resolves every selection case as specified: name, override, default, typo and every listed implementation. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Ports and adapters; plugin registries; how libraries let an embedding program declare and select alternatives at run time.
measures_of_success: Every switch works from configuration alone, no typo falls back silently, and a program that embeds the package selects an implementation without reading this repository. Standing conditions: Switching is a data change made while the program is deployed or run; declaring an alternative is one decorator; an unknown name fails with the choices; targets load lazily so an embedding program pays only for what it selects.
parameters: Solution id, implementation name per call, a context block, an environment variable, a deployment table.
inputs: Declarations in code, the records' selected cell, an optional selection table of module:Attribute targets.
outputs: The chosen implementation, and for a table its config class.
effects: Imports the chosen target; reads the records or a snapshot once.
usage_notes: The records' selected cell is the project default; let the metric decide it and leave it out of code.

name: Assemble parts by name
description: Lets one solution's implementation need another by name instead of by import, so configuration can swap a part and a missing or circular need fails when the program starts.
purpose: Build the parts of a program from validated names in dependency order, so each part depends on a solution and never on a particular implementation.
approach: Validate each name against the solution's listed implementations, load only modules that a record names, resolve each part through the cascade of explicit name, selections, environment, lock and package default, and build the parts in dependency order.
out_of_scope: Deciding which implementation is best, importing a module no record names, and reading the deployment table, the process environment or a parent folder's configuration; a name that is not listed is an error, never a fall-through.
milestones: 1. Assembly correctness: every offline case of the live assembler passes, hostile names, cycles, unmet needs and concurrent assembles included.
knowledge: Implementations depend on solutions, never on other implementations; a name is data, while an import path read from a file runs code nobody reviewed; a cycle or an unmet need is cheaper to find at startup than on the first call that reaches it. See docs/explanation/cross-dependency-by-name.md.
measures_of_success: Every offline case of the live assembler passes. Standing conditions: A hostile name, snapshot or parent configuration runs nothing; a cycle or a need nothing meets fails at startup naming the chain; the assembled system is frozen once built.
parameters: Assembler: scope, package_dir, modules, records, parent. AssemblyConfig: solutions, selections, options, selection_environ, consumer_environ, lock, circumstances. assemble(config, provided=...).
inputs: The package's scope and folder, the solutions to build, the consumer's selections, options and ready objects, and the records or packaged snapshot that name the implementations and each solution's default.
outputs: A frozen Assembly: the built part of each solution in dependency order, with the choice and reason line of each (choice, implementation, reasons); explain lists every layer of one solution.
effects: Imports a module only when a record of the package names it and its file lies inside the package folder; leaves sys.path unchanged; reads no environment beyond the mapping it is given; raises at startup on a cycle or an unmet need.
usage_notes: Declare each solution once as a Protocol with @solution, type a constructor parameter with it to need it, build one Assembler(scope, folder, modules=...) in the package and call assemble(AssemblyConfig(...)) at startup. See docs/how-to/assemble-by-name.md.
